description: Improvements measured after the first layered prototype, whole video R (2241 frames). Rounds alternated between before and after because load varied (load 4-9); a single round can be off by about 15%.
conditions: Same containment and metric as r-steps.json.

dedup.what: Before each graphics capture, SHA-256 of the page state (full outerHTML, every CSS rule including adoptedStyleSheets, form values, scroll, viewport). A state already captured becomes a hard link to the PNG on disk. Frames with canvas, video, iframe, object, embed, SVG image, unloaded img, loading fonts, running CSS animations, shadow DOM or cross-origin sheets are always captured.
dedup.check_mode: 1584 states, 657 repeats, 0 differing PNGs (byte-exact) when every frame is captured and compared
dedup.quality: SSIM 0.99698 (min 0.9917) against the layered render without dedup; a re-run of that render against itself gives 0.99723 (min 0.9919). 1920x1080: 0.99645.
dedup.version_lock: Patches the internal takeFrame export of @remotion/renderer; refuses to run on any version other than 4.0.536.

dirty_rects.what: Capture only the changed area of the graphics layer (Page.captureScreenshot with clip) and recompose in Node.
dirty_rects.detection: No pixel differed outside the clip in 2241 frames.
dirty_rects.why: Chrome rasterizes differently when the capture has a clip (rounded caption corners up to 255 in a channel of near-transparent pixels; shadow blur off by up to 3). Not fixed by disabling captureBeyondViewport or aligning the clip to 256 px.
dirty_rects.verdict: Slower overall than the plain PNG path and not pixel-exact. Consistent with Remotion removing Experimental.Clipper in 2024.

parallel_segments.what: Run 2 or 3 ffmpeg segment jobs at the same time.
parallel_segments.verdict: Wall -28% with 2 jobs, but CPU +20%. Kept as an option, default 1.

shared_memory_nvenc_for_graphics.what: renderMedia with shared-memory capture and h264_nvenc instead of a PNG sequence (graphics only, seg375)
